- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often over-optimistically forecasts upward; reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect caution.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope toward historical mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate upward trends in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.7 over last 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “low → high” transitions, model often misjudges momentum; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or peaks.
